reply_text:
GBrain is installed, wired into Hermes, and verified with real calls.

What's in place

  Version        gbrain 0.60.734.0 — pinned to the tag you named (`#v0.60.734.0`, commit a278ddf)
  Runtime        Bun 1.4.4 at /harness-state/.bun/bin/bun (gbrain's floor is 1.4.4)
  Source         /harness-state/gbrain-src/gbrain-0.60.734.0, installed via `bun install && bun link`
  Binary         /harness-state/.bun/bin/gbrain (on PATH)
  Brain          PGLite at /harness-state/.gbrain/brain.pglite, keyless, embeddings disabled
  Content root   /harness-state/.gbrain/content/a653bb7c-.../default
  Migrations     applied (v0.11.0, 0.14.0, 0.22.4, 0.28.0, 0.53.0); `gbrain doctor` reports status healthy, health_score 100
  Hermes wiring  mcp_servers.gbrain in ~/hermes/config.yaml → `hermes mcp test gbrain` connects in 2.0 s, 172 tools discovered

Two deviations from the guide, both deliberate:

  1. Install path. The doc's primary command (`bun install -g github:garrytan/gbrain#v0.60.734.0`) was refused by the security scanner — no network threat-intel in this unattended session, and single-query mode can't prompt for approval. I used the fallback the same doc specifies for exactly this case (`git clone` + `bun install && bun link`), plus a codeload tarball fetch since `git clone` was flagged too. Same tagged source, same result.
  2. `#stable` vs your pin. Docs say install at `#stable`, which today resolves to 0.60.737.0. Your explicit `#v0.60.734.0` won. Don't run `gbrain self-upgrade` — `doctor` will keep offering 0.60.737.0 and that leaves the pin.

Identity and instructions untouched: no SOUL.md changes, no new persona, no USER.md/HEARTBEAT.md, no API keys, no cron, no autopilot, no automatic capture. The only config edit is the MCP server entry; one memory entry notes the install.

Search mode — your call (this is the Step 3.5 decision)

GBrain auto-applied `conservative` because there's no chat/embedding key and no reranker:

                    Haiku 4.5     Sonnet 4.6    Opus 4.7
                    ($1/M)        ($3/M)        ($5/M)
    conservative    $40/mo        $120/mo       $200/mo
    balanced        $100/mo       $300/mo       $500/mo
    tokenmax        $200/mo       $600/mo       $1,000/mo

  (x10 for 100K queries/mo, /10 for 1K. 25x corner-to-corner spread. These are downstream model input
  costs; gbrain's own first-run report printed lower figures — $4/$80/$160, $10/$200/$400, $20/$400/$800.)

  1) conservative — 4K budget, 10 chunks. What's active now.
  2) balanced     — 12K budget, 25 chunks.
  3) tokenmax     — no budget, 50 chunks.

Unattended, so I left `conservative` in place rather than spend your money on a guess. Say which one and I'll run `gbrain config set search.mode <mode>` (verified with `gbrain search modes`).

Verification — real calls, both paths

  CLI remember → inserted fact #1 (provenance `install-check`, entity `gbrain install kestrel-marker`)
  CLI recall by entity → returned the fact
  CLI recall --grep in a fresh process → returned it (exact-substring only, see note below)
  gbrain search on a written page → retrieved by unique token, `keyword_hit: true`, evidence `keyword_exact`
  MCP remember through the same stdio server Hermes now spawns → inserted fact #2, status `committed`
  MCP recall (by entity, and by question) → returned fact #2 on a cold process
  CLI recall of the MCP-written fact → returned it, proving both writers share one brain

Test artifacts cleaned up: both facts forgotten, probe page soft-deleted. Brain is back to 0 pages, 0 facts — nothing invented about you is stored.

One behaviour to know: `remember`/`recall` and `search` are different stores. Facts go in via `remember` and come back via `recall`; pages come back via `search`. With no embedding key, `recall --grep` is exact-substring, so "kestrel" misses "kestrel-marker", and every recall carries a `degraded_recall` notice (semantic search didn't run — that's the keyless choice, not a failure).

Defaults now in effect, off-switches in case you want them

  Free upkeep while a gbrain session is open — off: `gbrain config set maintenance.auto false`
  Conversation archive, one redacted page per conversation per day — off: `gbrain transcripts archive off`

Restart Hermes to use the tools in a session — MCP servers are read at start, so this conversation doesn't see them yet.
